title: LRU
subtitle: Data structures behind O(1) Least Recently Used eviction, LFU vs W-TinyLFU, and Redis approximated LRU.
keyTakeaways: A textbook O(1) LRU cache combines a Hash Map (`key -> Node*`) for O(1) lookups with a Doubly Linked List (`head = MRU, tail = LRU`) for O(1) promotion and eviction.
Pure LRU suffers from 'Scan Pollution': a one-time bulk scan of cold items flushes out genuinely popular items; LFU or W-TinyLFU solves this by tracking access frequency.
Redis does not use a doubly linked list for LRU (to save 16 bytes of pointer overhead per key); instead, it uses approximated sampling of N random keys.

sections.heading: 1. Architectural Fundamentals & Core Mechanics
sections.body: Every `get(key)` or `put(key, val)` in an LRU cache looks up the node in a hash table in O(1) time and splices that node to the `head` (Most Recently Used) of a doubly linked list in O(1) time. When capacity is reached, the node at the `tail` (Least Recently Used) is unlinked and removed from the hash map.
bullets: **Core Architectural Principle**: A textbook O(1) LRU cache combines a Hash Map (`key -> Node*`) for O(1) lookups with a Doubly Linked List (`head = MRU, tail = LRU`) for O(1) promotion and eviction.

**Problem Space & Invariants**: Pure LRU suffers from 'Scan Pollution': a one-time bulk scan of cold items flushes out genuinely popular items; LFU or W-TinyLFU solves this by tracking access frequency.
**System Boundary**: Operates across client network dispatch, gateway queuing, thread execution pools, and persistent storage I/O.

sections.heading: 2. Architectural Patterns & Implementation Topologies
sections.body: Distributed architectures apply specific implementation patterns and topologies for LRU:
bullets: **LRU (Least Recently Used)**: Provides adapts immediately to sudden recency shifts (e.g., breaking news); simple o(1) mechanics. Best suited for Session caches, recency-driven news feeds, and general application caching.

**LFU / W-TinyLFU (Frequency-Aware Eviction)**: Provides scan-resistant; retains consistently popular keys even during one-off read bursts. Best suited for Product catalogs, CDN edge caches, and skewed power-law Zipfian workloads.

Lock Contention in Multi-Threaded In-Process Caches: Because every *read* mutates the linked list pointers, a global mutex turns concurrent reads into a serial bottleneck. Production libraries (like Java Caffeine or Go Ristretto) buffer read events in lock-free ring buffers and apply promotions asynchronously.
Scan Pollution Problem: If capacity is 10,000 items and a user runs a pagination job reading 10,000 one-off cold items, pure LRU evicts all 10,000 hot items.
`allkeys-lru` vs `volatile-lru`: `allkeys-lru` evicts any key when RAM is full; `volatile-lru` only evicts keys that have an explicit TTL set (preserving permanent state).
`allkeys-lfu` (Morris Counter): Uses those same 24 header bits to store a 16-bit last-decrement time and an 8-bit logarithmic frequency counter (0–255) with time decay.

sections.heading: 3. Production Strengths: Where & How to Apply
sections.body: Production deployments apply LRU across targeted operational scenarios:
bullets: **Where to Use: High-Impact Scenarios**: Optimal for Session caches, recency-driven news feeds, and general application caching, suited for environments requiring Adapts immediately to sudden recency shifts (e.g., breaking news); simple O(1) mechanics.

**Where to Use: High-Throughput Scenarios**: Recommended for Product catalogs, CDN edge caches, and skewed power-law Zipfian workloads, where Scan-resistant; retains consistently popular keys even during one-off read bursts.

**How to Use: Engineering Implementation**: Maintaining two 64-bit pointers (`prev`, `next`) per key across 100 million keys in Redis would waste 1.6 GB of RAM. Always establish explicit thresholds, measurement baselines, and automated monitoring.
**Architectural Leverage**: Provides predictable resource boundaries, bounds blast radius, and optimizes cost per transaction.

sections.heading: 4. Failure Modes & Trade-Offs: When to Avoid
sections.body: Improper implementation of LRU introduces operational bottlenecks and failure modes:
bullets: **Where to Avoid: Trade-Off Bottlenecks**: Avoid when constraints cannot tolerate: vulnerable to cache pollution from sequential scans or one-time bulk queries.
**Where to Avoid: Complexity Ceiling**: Avoid when operational requirements do not justify: requires frequency decay tuning so formerly popular items don't stay stuck in memory forever.
**Catastrophic Failure Modes**: Uncalibrated parameters can trigger queue exhaustion, thread starvation, cascading retry storms, and tail latency amplification.
**Operational Overhead**: Requires continuous observability (p95/p99 latency tracking, saturation alerts, and distributed tracing across hop boundaries).

sections.heading: 5. Staff+ Engineering Verdict & Interview Playbook
sections.body: Technical guidelines and evaluation criteria for LRU:
bullets: **Staff+ Golden Rule**: Redis does not use a doubly linked list for LRU (to save 16 bytes of pointer overhead per key); instead, it uses approximated sampling of N random keys.

**Staff+ Interview Playbook**: Be ready to code an O(1) LRU Cache from scratch using a HashMap + Doubly Linked List, and follow up by explaining how concurrent in-memory caches avoid lock contention on the linked list during reads.
